title: Mitigating Social Biases in Language Models through Unlearning
findings: The unlearning methods, especially Negation via Task Vector (TV), effectively reduced stereotypical biases related to religion in language models like LLaMA-2 7B and OPT. For instance, the TV method lowered the CrowS-Pairs bias score in the religion category for LLaMA-2 7B from 0.793 to 0.622. Qualitative analysis on prompts about Sikhs showed that the base model produced biased stereotypes, while the TV-debiased model generated more neutral and factual text. However, applying the debiasing methods too strongly, particularly PCGU, led to a degradation in text quality and coherence.

measurement_description: Detection and mitigation of social biases and stereotypes related to religious groups. This was measured quantitatively using the 'Religion' sub-category of the CrowS-Pairs dataset and qualitatively through open-ended text generation prompts about religious groups from the BOLD dataset.
